subject: Trapping Web for Fish in Wetland Situation

messages.author: 6510ebbe3488de85
messages.subject: Trapping Web for Fish in Wetland Situation
parts:
Dear List:

I have a need to develop a sampling method to collect density and diversity
data of fishes from shallow wetlands of the Florida Everglades. We will be
conducting an extensive foodweb study and need population-level data of
small fish (<80mm) and crayfish in treatment and control plots.

Initially, I conceived of using a Capture-Recapture method, but after
extensive review and testing, we cannot individually mark these fish
because they are too small. We must batch-mark all animals we catch by fin
nicking. This to me negates the ability to conduct most Capture-Recapture
techniques.

Given our limitations, I believe that a Trapping Web could be useful to
collect our needed density and diversity information. We will be employing
passive samplers to collect fish over several days (minnow traps). In
addition, we will be surrounding our study area by a drift fence to
prohibit gains/losses of animals. Coupled with our short sampling
timeframe, this should satisfy the closed-population requirement.

The Trapping Web has 3 necessary assumptions (see Buckland et al. 1993):
all center animals are captured, no migration & small relative movements,
and accurate trap distance measurements.

I believe we can satisfy most of these conditions; however, we have a
limited amount of information about these fish movements, but believe the
range is small within a few days.

The help I am seeking would be any field stories or examples whereby the
Trapping Web was used, 1) in an aquatic situation for fishes and/or 2) if
this indeed is the MOST appropriate assessment technique for our situation,
and if not 3) please let us know what analytical technique you believe
would be more robust, etc.

Best regards,

Mac Kobza

Aquatic Ecologist
Everglades Division
South Florida Water Management District
rko...@sfwmd.gov
